source: Minchat Shai on Gen 41:50 (the chilufim; Rav Paalim; the Great Masorah's note)
claim_en: u-le-yosef YULAD ('and to Joseph were BORN two sons'): MS found ALL his books with qamatz — and the printed variance-lists rule that reading BEN NAPHTALI's, with BEN ASHER reading patach (Rav Paalim: 'patach for Ben Asher, qamatz for Ben Naphtali'). SNAPSHOT writes the PATACH — the stream with BEN ASHER against Ben Naphtali and against every book MS saw: the corpus's SECOND Ben Asher/Ben Naphtali station (after yehi or, Gen 1:3) — and the stream sides with Ben Asher both times.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 41:14 (the Ramah; the Meiri; the Zohar; against the printers)
claim_en: va-yeritzuhu ('and they RUSHED him from the pit'): some prints wrote it doubly lean and the Great Masorah's note misled Minchat Kohen; every precise manuscript, the Meiri, and the Ramah rule FULL yod, LEAN vav — and the Zohar reads the lean vav itself: who ran him out? the Holy One — 'for none binds and none looses but He.' Once in the Torah.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 41:2 quoting the Ramah
claim_en: va-tirena ('and they GRAZED'): 'two, doubly full — yod before the nun and final he' — the dream's grazing and its retelling (41:2, 41:18), census exact.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

claim_en: The swallow-verb FLIPS between dream and retelling: va-tivlana (41:7) written with final he and the bent nun; va-tivlan (41:24) without the he, the nun straightened — the Ramah rules both stations, each once in the stream (the second asserted).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 41:7 quoting the Ramah
claim_en: ve-ha-meleot ('the FULL ears'): lean yod, full vav — 'and every other fullness-word in the Torah is lean except this one'; the books that write 41:22's melet full are in error (the Ramah: 'the precise texts and the Masorah dispute them'). The one full token checked.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 41:26 (the Hilleli and Yerushalmi codices; the Ramah)
claim_en: sheva PAROT ha-tovot ('the seven GOOD COWS', the interpretation's first word-pair): the Hilleli codex lean, the Yerushalmi full — and here the stream sides WITH the Hilleli: parot lean, marked unique-and-lean by the Masorah and the Ramah. The lean skeleton collides across the Torah with the EUPHRATES (perat — 2:14, 15:18, Deut 1:7, 11:24) and with Joseph's own blessing, ben PORAT ×2 (49:22): the cows, the river, and the fruitful bough share one skeleton, seven tokens.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 41:27 quoting the Ramah
claim_en: ve-ha-raot ('the EVIL cows', the interpretation's second mention): 'every evil-plural in the Torah is FULL except TWO lean' — this token, and lo tihye achare rabim LE-RAOT ('you shall not follow the many to evil', Exod 23:2, named): the lean evils are Pharaoh's cows and the perverted court.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 41:23 quoting the Ramah
claim_en: achare-hen ('after THEM', feminine): the form's WHOLE Torah career is this chapter's five tokens (41:3, 6, 19, 27, 30) — and the Ramah's own exception stands at 41:23: the one achare-HEM with mem inside the same dream-cycle (asserted). A word whose entire life is one chapter, minus one letter-slip the Masorah itself flagged.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 41:45 (the Ramah; the Meiri; Yerushalmi Megilla; tractate Soferim; the old chumash)
claim_en: The naming verse writes TWO two-word names: tzafnat paneach — 'they are ONE name written and read as two words' (the Ramah), the old chumash adding they must share one line; and poti fera — two words with NO maqqef between them (the precise books, Yerushalmi Megilla, Soferim). SNAPSHOT carries each as two unjoined tokens (poti's no-maqqef checked; all four tokens asserted) — the instrumented mirror of Potiphar-the-one-word (G62-01).
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 41:45 and 41:54 (most Sephardic precise books)
claim_en: Two more wheel-rulings: the ayin-syllable of far'o at the naming (41:45) and the he of ha-aratzot ('all the LANDS', 41:54) — most precise books rule GALGAL on both; SNAPSHOT writes the munach at each: galgal-class stations 8 and 9, the stream's munach-camp membership now nine stations wide (both checked via the stroke in-stream, joined to the class file).
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 41:50 (the Masorah)
claim_en: u-le-yosef ('and to Joseph') — exactly TWICE in the Torah, both Torah-side: two sons born before the famine (41:50), and Moses' blessing 'and to Joseph he said: blessed of the LORD is his land' (Deut 33:13): the Kitzur — who joins the community in its trouble lives to see its comfort.
middah: E7 (the concordance pair — the same wording at two seats, the Kitzur's reading at narrative strength)

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 41:5 (the Masorah)
claim_en: be-qane echad ('on ONE STALK') — exactly THREE in the Torah: the good ears twice (41:5, 41:22) and the made MENORAH's cups (Exod 37:19): the Kitzur — plenty is light for the world; only the good ears grow on one stalk, and the lamp shares their phrase.
middah: E7 (the concordance pair — the same wording at two seats, the Kitzur's reading at narrative strength)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 41:7/9/13/33/43/48/52/57 (the chapter's file)
claim_en: The chapter's pointing-and-accent file: ha-beriot ('the healthy ears') with the bet DAGESHED (checked); anyi ('my affliction') with the ayin in qamatz alone, chazaq's zayin in patach, the was/were pair (hayu 41:48 / haya 41:53 — one of the Masorah's three such pairs, the Ezekiel sign named; both asserted); and the named file: yere (41:33) end-stressed against the custom — the Masorah's 'none other so'; be-mirkevet (41:43) — 'the only chiriq of its word'; ka-asher unjoined with the shin stroked (41:13); the et of 41:9 in segol; Chizkuni's four resh-tzere hollow-cows note (41:19).
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

claim_en: A THREE-WAY STANDOFF OVER A WORD THAT HAS NO SECOND SEAT TO ARBITRATE IT. The herald's cry at 41:43, the untranslated word ‹אַבְרֵךְ› ('avrekh'), is read by the chain as great ‹אָב› ('av,' father) in wisdom and tender ‹רַךְ› ('rakh,' tender) in years, while Onkelos decides it as a title of office - THIS IS THE FATHER TO THE KING. Machine-checked: the word is a HAPAX in the entire Torah, standing exactly once, at this verse. There is no other seat anywhere in the corpus against which to test any of the three readings, and the machine can state that as a fact rather than a suspicion - which is precisely why three readings stand and none is settled.
middah: ink (the herald's word a hapax — three readings, none settled)

claim_en: AN INK CONTRAST WHOSE NEAR LEG IS EXACT AND WHOSE FAR LEG CANNOT BE OPENED HERE - GRADED SEPARATELY. The chain contrasts the spelling of Pharaoh's troubled spirit at 41:8, ‹וַתִּפָּעֶם› ('vatipa'em'), written with ONE letter tav, against the doubled-tav form at Daniel 2:1, ‹וַתִּתְפָּעֶם› ('vatitpa'em'), and hangs three readings on the difference plus a timing rule. THE GENESIS LEG IS EXACT: machine-checked, the single-tav form stands exactly once in the whole Torah, at this verse. THE DANIEL LEG IS NOT OPENED: Daniel lies outside this corpus, which carries the Torah only, so the comparison's other end is declared unopened rather than confirmed or denied. One leg proved, one leg named as unreachable - the grade attaches to each separately.
middah: ink (the single-tav spelling checked; the Daniel leg unopened)

claim_en: THE SEAM BETWEEN TWO SEVEN-YEAR TERMS IS PRICED AT A VERB, AND BOTH VERBS ARE IN OUR INK. The years of plenty 'were completed' ‹וַתִּכְלֶינָה› ('vatikhlena') at 41:53, read as emerging whole; the years of famine 'began' ‹וַתְּחִלֶּינָה› ('vateḥilena') at 41:54, read as entering already ill - hunger on the first day though they had eaten on the last. Verified at the ink: the two verses stand adjacent, the two forms open their verses in the same feminine-plural shape, and the consonantal difference the reading rests on is present exactly as described. The economy's two regimes are distinguished by one letter.

check.note: Adjacent verses whose opening verbs differ by one consonant, carrying the reading that the plenty ended whole and the famine began already ill.

middah: ink (completed against began — the two verbs' forms; the readings beside)

claim_en: A STANDING LAW RESTS ON THIS UNIT'S OWN INK, AND THE SEAT IS THE PROOF. The rule that intercourse is forbidden in a time of famine is grounded in 41:50 - 'and to Joseph were born two sons BEFORE the year of famine came.' Verified in the ink: the verse carries the temporal clause 'before the year of famine came' exactly, and the births are placed on the prior side of it. A narrative time-stamp is doing legal work; a credit standing since gen_16 named this verse as its forward seat, and the seat is now occupied.

check.note: A dietary-adjacent abstinence law grounded in a narrative clause placing two births before a famine's onset.

middah: plain (before-the-famine-year read as the famine-relations rule's source)

claim_en: TWO TORAH PASSAGES ARE LEARNED FROM A WICKED KING'S WORDING, AND AN INFERENCE FORM IS TAKEN FROM HIS PRONOUN. Reish Lakish holds that the restrictive particle ‹רַק› ('rak,' only) caps whatever precedes it, and derives the reading of two later verses from Pharaoh's 'ONLY the throne will I be greater than you' at 41:40 - so 'you shall be ONLY above' and 'you shall be holy' both keep God's greatness and sanctity above Israel's, exactly as Pharaoh's clause keeps his above Joseph's. Beside it, an argument from the lesser to the greater is run off 'I am Pharaoh' at 41:44: if the 'I' of flesh and blood conferred that honor, how much more the 'I' of the Holy One. A particle rule and an inference form, both sourced from a speech the tradition itself calls wicked.

check.note: A restrictive-particle rule and an a-fortiori form derived from the wording of a character the tradition condemns.

middah: E2 (only caps what precedes it — two later verses read from Pharaoh's clause; the I-am a-fortiori, E5, beside)

claim_en: A REFUSAL IS PAID OUT LIMB BY LIMB IN THE INK OF THE NEXT CHAPTER. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel matches six body parts that did not transgress in the earlier scene to six honors in this one: the mouth that did not kiss is repaid 'at your word shall my people be fed'; the body that did not touch, the linen garments; the neck that did not bend, the gold chain; the hands that did not grope, the signet ring; the feet that did not stride, the chariot; the thought that did not think, being called wise. The exact mirror of the three-slanders-three-repayments table this corpus already carries, and a worked example of the tradition auditing a reward against an itemized restraint.

check.note: A six-row body-part table matching an earlier restraint to this unit's honors, one for one.

middah: E27 (six restraints repaid by six honours — the itemized mirror)

claim_en: THE INTERPRETATION IS HELD TO MAKE THE EVENT, AND THE DENIAL IS RECORDED BESIDE IT. From 'as he interpreted to us, SO IT WAS' (41:13) the chain derives that dreams follow the mouth, with the case of the woman whose broken-beam dream one master read as a son born and living and his students, in his absence, as a husband buried - 'you have eliminated a man.' Carried as a RECORDED DISPUTE, not a ruling: R. Yoḥanan excepts wine, and R. Abahu denies the premise outright - the content of dreams makes no difference. The operative rule the whole chapter runs on is preserved together with the opinion that it is worthless.

check.note: A rule that interpretation actualizes a dream, preserved alongside a flat denial of the rule.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

claim_en: THE UNIT'S SEVEN-YEAR TERM IS ITSELF DISPUTED FOUR WAYS, AND THE DISPUTE IS NOT A WORD-CENSUS. Asked how many famine years the dream should have produced, R. Yehuda says fourteen (what Pharaoh saw), R. Neḥemya twenty-eight (adding what he said to Joseph), the Rabbis forty-two (adding Joseph's repetition back) - against R. Yosei ben Ḥanina, who holds the famine actually lasted TWO years and ceased when Jacob descended, resuming only in the prophet's day. Opened rather than credited, and graded honestly: these are counts of what a telling should generate, not counts of tokens in the text, so the machine cannot adjudicate them - it records that the term its own operators carry is a disputed quantity in the chain.

check.note: A four-way numeric dispute over a narrative term, explicitly not a word census and therefore not machine-adjudicable.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

claim_en: THE WRONG READING IS RECORDED IN FULL, AND THE ORDER OF ATTEMPTS IS READ AS DESIGN. The magicians did interpret: seven daughters born and seven buried, seven kingdoms conquered and seven provinces rebelling - preserved verbatim as the failed reading, giving the machine a negative control rather than a silence. And the sequence is read as engineered: they were permitted to exhaust him first so that Joseph's interpretation could not be met with 'had you asked us first' - the same engineered-order mechanism this corpus already carries from the prison block. A wrong answer kept on the record because keeping it is what makes the right one demonstrable.

check.note: A failed interpretation preserved verbatim, with the order of attempts read as deliberate design.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

claim_en: THE TRANSLATION REFUSES A FOREIGN NAME AND WITHHOLDS A PRIESTLY TITLE. Where the verse gives Joseph the Egyptian name ‹צָפְנַת פַּעְנֵחַ› ('Tzafenat Paneaḥ'), Onkelos does not carry it over but TRANSLATES it - 'the man to whom hidden things are revealed' - stating the office instead of transliterating the name. At the same two seats the father-in-law's title ‹כֹּהֵן› ('kohen,' priest) is rendered ‹רַבָּא› ('rabba,' chief), the priesthood withheld from the idolatrous cult. Two different guards in one clause: a name dissolved into a function, and a sacral word denied to a foreign shrine.

check.note: A foreign name translated rather than transliterated, and a priestly title downgraded to a civil one at both its seats.

middah: ink (the received translation's rendering)

claim_en: THREE DEMEANINGS IN ONE CLAUSE, AND AN EGYPTIAN STATUTE CITED AS WRITTEN LAW. The butler's 'a Hebrew lad, a slave' at 41:12 is read as three separate slurs - a lad meaning a fool, a Hebrew meaning an enemy tongue, a slave meaning one who by Pharaoh's own statute books may not reign and may not wear the royal bracelets. 'Cursed are the wicked, who do not perform a complete goodness.' The chain has the elevation clear a legal obstacle it states as positive foreign law, and it audits the confession's motive too: seeing the king near death, the butler calculated that a successor might not keep him.

check.note: A three-part slur read out of one clause, with a foreign statute cited as the legal obstacle the elevation must clear.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

claim_en: A PROPHETIC FACULTY IS DECLARED ABSENT, AND THE ABSENCE IS CARRIED AS MACHINE STATE. Explaining how Jacob 'SAW there was grain in Egypt' without being there, the chain answers that from the day Joseph was taken THE DIVINE SPIRIT LEFT HIM - he would see without seeing and hear without hearing. The claim is not decorative: it is a state entered at an earlier block and still holding here, and it is the reason the same passage can read his 'go down' as an unwitting prophecy. Around it the section builds the administration that finds the brothers - names and fathers' names written at the gates, the notes brought at evening, all storehouses shut but one.

check.note: A faculty declared lost at an earlier block and still in force here, used to explain an unwitting prophecy.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

claim_en: THE ONE PLACE THE PLENTY IS DESCRIBED AS ADMINISTRATION RATHER THAN ABUNDANCE. Where the verse has the earth producing 'by handfuls' at 41:47 and the chain reads the handfuls as reaping straight to the mill and as savings, Onkelos moves both subject and sense: THE INHABITANTS OF THE LAND STORED UP grain for storehouses. The yield becomes a human act of storage. A genuine semantic divergence, and the only seat in the chapter where the translation makes the abundance into a program rather than a gift - which is exactly the register the unit's storage operators run in.

check.note: A verse's subject moved from the ground's yield to a human act of storage, diverging from the chain's reading at the same seat.

middah: ink (the received translation's rendering)

claim_en: THE FAMINE IS GIVEN AN ORDER OF ARRIVAL, READ OFF ONE WORD, AND A CONDITION IS ATTACHED TO THE GRAIN. 'The famine was on the FACE of all the earth' (41:56) is read to mean it began with the WEALTHY, since only the moneyed have a face to show. And 'what he says to you, do' (41:55) is read as a compulsion to circumcise before buying, with the people appealing to Pharaoh and Pharaoh answering that they were warned through seven years of plenty and stored nothing - to which they reply that what they stored rotted: 'if he decrees on grain and it rots, perhaps he will decree on us.' A distribution rule and a conversion condition, both extracted from the administration of a food supply.

check.note: An order of arrival for a famine derived from one word, plus a religious condition attached to the sale of grain.

middah: plain (on-the-face read as the wealthy first; what-he-says-do as the circumcision condition)

claim_en: THE FAMINE-YEARS BAN. Reish Lakish reads the birth notice's timestamp — 'two sons born BEFORE the famine year came' — as conduct law: marital relations forbidden in famine years, with the baraita's rider excepting the childless. Filed F-122, auto-seated (round 32, the betrothal block).
middah: plain (the famine-years ban from the birth notice's timestamp — Taanit 11a)

claim_en: DREAMS FOLLOW THE MOUTH. The interpretation binds — as-he-interpreted-so-it-was the source, with Rava's must-fit cap and the twenty-four-interpreter experiment recorded. Filed F-183, auto-seated (round 40, the conduct block).
middah: plain (dreams follow the mouth — as-he-interpreted-so-it-was; Berakhot 55b)
